threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand on the right on escalators and look confused when everyone else zooms past on the left.
Saw a guy on the 333 talking about how he lost his shoes in a kebab shop brawl. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids trading Pokémon cards in the playground while their parents sipped beers nearby. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kiez langos shop serving Hungarian street food at 3 AM, while the techno floors filter out your weekend woes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they roll their eyes at the latest BART delays while casually sipping a coffee from Philz, not even fazed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy conducting a pet psychic reading on the 49 bus. The dog seemed to nod in agreement about the traffic delays. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' means non-stop nightlife. They miss the quiet cafes where locals disappear with a book every afternoon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they still call it 'Parc Güell' instead of 'el Parc del Güell'—locals just drop the article, you know?

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check Google Maps for the bus routes. Locals just know which one goes where without missing a beat.
Last week on the 35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old Soul II Soul tracks. Surprisingly, we all joined in. Brixton never sleeps, not even at night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I was at the park when two kids started negotiating a candy trade in Turkish, switching to German as if it was nothing. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Turkish bakery that sells fresh simit right next to a vegan café. The scent of sesame and espresso is unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively know to carry an extra pair of shoes on a rainy day, just in case the wet BART platform becomes a slip-n-slide.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full business attire swap his briefcase for a dog leash as he jumped off Muni—only in San Francisco!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all the bars close at 2am, but plenty of locals head to the hidden ones in the alleys when the clock strikes. It’s a whole secret scene.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their bewilderment at finding a bus that doesn’t have a route number, just a name. Classic rookie mistake.
